about: Addresses and pairing codes under core version 0's rules (spec/v0/core.md sections 2 and 5): https only, prefix msfp-pair-0. Every other case of vectors/history/test-draft-strict.json holds for core 0 unchanged. Generated by tools/vectors.

mediaNames: file and track names in media URLs (MSFP Media fetching section 1, https://github.com/msfp-io/msfp-media/blob/main/spec/v0/fetching.md). bases: the discovery document's base (spec/v0/core.md, the discovery document).
destinations: IP addresses a server connects to for a peer by default (valid), or refuses (spec/v0/core.md section 3.3; also the test draft's section 3.2).

uncallableAddresses: the address a server that sends inbound false must have, https://msfp-<26>.invalid, the 26 characters being 16 bytes in lowercase base32 with the unused bits zero (spec/v0/core.md section 5.2).

helloVersions: hello bodies (text) and what a receiver keeps of their versions (output: core, and each known part by name; spec/v0/core.md sections 2.3 and 10.2), or a bad body (valid false). A number that isn't an integer is valid I-JSON, and is ignored in a version list.

languageCodes: a media server's language code (text) and the tag a server sends for it (output), or none (valid false): an ISO 639-2 code, /B or /T, of a language with an ISO 639-1 code sent as that code, the rest kept, in BCP 47's case conventions; und, mul, zxx and mis not sent (MSFP Media base sections 2.4 and 2.3, https://github.com/msfp-io/msfp-media/blob/main/spec/v0/base.md).

titlePages: pages of titles (MSFP Media listing section 3.1, https://github.com/msfp-io/msfp-media/blob/main/spec/v0/listing.md, as MSFP's catalog carries it). Input: changes (a changes answer or a whole-list one), titles and gone (how many keys the page holds), bytes (the answer body's size), remain (whole list: whether titles remain after the page on the owning server), after (the request's), lastKey (the page's last title key), next (absent when the answer has none). Output: valid (the owning server may send it: at most 5,000 keys, titles and gone together; at most 3 MiB, 3,145,728 bytes, of JSON; in a whole list, next is the last key exactly when titles remain), and caller: what the caller does with it whatever valid says: fail (past the carrier's bound for an answer, MSFP's 4 MiB, 4,194,304 bytes: MSFP core section 3), stop (next absent, empty, or not greater than after in byte order), or ask on.

titleOffer and titleRequests: the titles request as the owning server reads it (MSFP Media listing sections 3, 3.3 and 3.6). titleOffer is what it holds: the libraries the caller may see (visible; Lh9, which holds titles too, isn't one of them) and its titles, each in the libraries listed, with what under goes by (an episode's season, its place.season; a track's album; an album's artists). Each case of titleRequests: parts, the content parts in use between the two; body, the request. valid false: 404 not-found, the request refused (a body that isn't valid JSON, libraries that isn't an array of strings, kind or under that isn't a string, kind that isn't a token, under or after over 512 bytes, since that isn't an integer). valid true: output is what it lists, in byte order of key, of the titles after after: each key and its library (of the requested libraries the caller may see, or of all it may see when libraries is absent, the first in byte order), the titles of the kind kind names (a token that is no kind of a part in use: none), and those directly under the key under names (a film: its extras; a series: its seasons, its extras, its episodes keyed by an absolute number; a season: its episodes keyed under it or by their TMDB episode ID with that place.season, its extras; an album: its tracks; an artist: its albums; under is the exact string, never checked against the key forms); then mayBeChanges: whether the answer may hold only changes (since above 0, and no under: with under it is always the whole list).
opaqueKeyParts: the opaque parts of title keys, a local title's identifier or an extra's part after x/ (MSFP Media listing section 4.2): 1 to 64 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -, compared byte for byte.

localImages: the image of a local title (MSFP Media listing section 4.4), on three sides. request: the owning server's answer (status, type: the problem's type) to the image request body, given parts (the content parts on between the two servers) and offered (the titles it offers the caller, with whether their description says image true): 404 not-supported with no content part with local titles on; 400 invalid-request for a malformed body; 404 not-found for a title not offered, not local, of a part that is off, of a kind without an image (only films, series, artists and albums have one), or without an image; else 200. answer: the viewer's server's check of the answer body (body), {"ticket"}, the ticket 1 to 64 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -: valid with the ticket and the URL it builds from it and the owning server's stream root (streamRoot, MSFP Media fetching section 1; MSFP media section 1), <stream root><ticket>/image; or refused (valid false), no image. The answer carries no URL: a url member is unknown, ignored. image: the image's first bytes (hex) and its whole length (size): valid when size is at most 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes), the content is a JPEG (FF D8 FF) or a PNG (the 8-byte signature), whatever any Content-Type, and the header gives a width and a height of 1 to 4,096 pixels (a PNG's IHDR, a JPEG's frame header SOF0 to SOF15 but DHT, JPG and DAC); format jpeg or png.

openTokens: values of open fields (MSFP Media base section 3). A token is 1 to 32 characters of a-z 0-9 . _ -. In a fact (titles, play's answer) a token is kept as it is, known or not (valid true), never turned into another value; a value that isn't a token is malformed (valid false): dropped alone when the member is optional, with the entry holding it (a copy, a track, an extra) when the member is required. In a request, an unknown token is ignored where the field is a hint and refused where it names what to serve: 409 delivery-refused for a delivery, 409 target-refused for a target (a remux's media type, a transcode codec, a range; MSFP Media playing sections 2.1, 2.2 and 2.7); only a value that isn't a token gets 400.

openMediaTypes: values of media-type fields (MSFP Media base section 3): an IANA-form media type, lowercase, exactly one /, no parameters, each half starting with a letter or a digit, at most 127 characters of a-z 0-9 . + - _ /. Kept as it is, known or not (valid true); otherwise malformed (valid false), handled as openTokens says. Libraries and titles carry no kind (MSFP Media listing sections 2 and 3): a kind member is unknown, ignored; kind is a filter of the titles request (titleRequests).
